MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  May 22, 2012

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 7:30 PM in the Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Bird.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL (7:30 PM)

PRESENT:  Mayor Bird, Mayor Pro Tem Goodhart, Councilmember Humphrey,
  Councilmember Perkins, Councilmember Rea

ABSENT:  None

ALSO PRESENT:  City Manager Smith, Police Chief Dreiling, Public Works Director Rigg, City
  Treasurer Sherwood, City Attorney Hogin, Asst. to City Manager Davis,
  Asst./Deputy City Clerk Kroneberger

CEREMONIAL MATTERS

  •  Swearing-In of Police Sergeant Luke Hellinga and Corporal Dave Blitz (Chief Dreiling)

Police Chief Dreiling introduced Luke Hellinga, who began his career with the City of Palos
Verdes Estates in 2001, and Dave Blitz, who came to the PVE Police Department in 1990.

He administered the promotional oath to Sergeant Hellinga and Corporal Blitz. Sergeant
Hellinga’s wife pinned on his badge, accompanied by their newborn son. Corporal Blitz’ wife
pinned on his badge, accompanied by their daughter.

The officers introduced their families; and Mayor Bird and Council congratulated the promoted
officers.

MAYOR'S REPORT - MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

CONSENT AGENDA (ITEMS 1 - 7a-c)

On motion of Councilmember Humphrey, seconded by Councilmember Rea, Council approved
CONSENT AGENDA (Items 1 – 7a-c) by unanimous oral vote.

9.  RESOLUTION R12-12; APPROVING THE ANNUAL REPORT AND SETTING THE
  RATE FOR THE SEWER USER FEE RATE TO FINANCE THE FY 2012-13
  PROGRAM OF SANITARY SEWER IMPROVEMENTS

City Manager Smith confirmed public notice has been given. She reported this hearing is to review
and establish the sewer user fee rate for FY12-13, which is the final year of the ten-year
authorization, which was first approved in 2003 after a public process. She said the fee appears on
property tax bills and is collected at same time. The fee is based on water consumption, using the 3
lowest months of water use. For the FY12-13 fee calculation, the months of January, February, and
March were determined to be the lowest water consumption months of 2011. Each parcel’s water
use is averaged to determine each property’s annual estimated sewer use. 1,098,000 sewer units
are estimated based on current consumption.

Under the ordinance that established the fee, the maximum rate allowed is $1.36/unit; however, it is
recommended that Council approves $.95/unit for FY 12-13 to generate a total estimated sewer
fund balance of $1.043 million. Last year, the rate was $1.00/unit with the average sewer user fee
being $208 per single-family home. This year, the average cost will be $207 per parcel. However,
each parcel's fee will vary; it could be higher or lower depending on water usage calculated for
each parcel.

City Manager Smith said the FY12-13 program involves completion of the Rocky Point Sewer
Pump Station and design of redundant sewer mains proposed for construction in FY13-14, which
will be funded by sewer fund balance. At the end of FY13-14, all identified projects will be
completed. Any sewer funds left will be used for future sewer repairs.

Councilmember Rea confirmed with City Manager Smith that $.95/unit is the lowest rate
established over the last ten years. $.97/unit was the prior lowest unit rate (FY 08-09) per City
Manager Smith. The expected revenue of $1,043,000 is comparable to that generated in this current

Mayor Bird opened the public hearing, and having no public wishing to speak, closed the public
hearing.

On motion of Councilmember Rea, seconded by Councilmember Perkins, Council adopted
Resolution R12-12; Approving the Annual Report and Setting the Rate for the Sewer User Fee Rate
to Finance the FY 2012-13 Program of Sanitary Sewer Improvements by unanimous oral vote.

NEW BUSINESS

Safety Committee member interviews in Adjourned Session before the Regular Meeting.

DEMANDS

11.  DEMANDS OF MAY 22, 2012

On motion of Councilmember Goodhart, seconded by Councilmember Perkins, Council approved
payment of Motion #1 – Payroll Warrant of May 11, 2012, totaling $212,674.76, and Motion #2 –
Warrant Register of May 22, 2012, totaling $263,295.58 by unanimous oral vote.

MAYOR& CITY COUNCILMEMBERS' REPORTS

Mayor Bird reported on his attendance at the South Bay Police and Fire Medal of Valor luncheon
on May 10th with Chief Dreiling; who was congratulated, a past honoree himself, on the occasion
of his retirement.

He reported on his attendance at the Capitol Comes to Campus event sponsored by PVP Council of
PTAs with Councilmember Perkins on Friday, May 18th and Saturday, May 19th; a program to
encourage participation in government to prepare knowledgeable and experienced future voters,
and he invited students to come to Council meetings to observe. On May 20th, the Mayor patrolled
the PVE coastline with PVE Reserves officers and thanked them for their service.

The Mayor also participated in Ridgecrest Middle School’s Career Day on May 21st.

Councilmember Rea reported on his attendance on April 30th at the Joint Powers Insurance
Authority Executive Committee Retreat and would attend their regular monthly meeting on May
23rd, and would provide insurance rates information at Budget hearing on the 24th.

 Councilmember Rea reported on his attendance at the Friendship Circle Honors event with his son
on May 20th; he presented a certificate of recognition to a PVHS student volunteer.

He commented on a Neighborhood Watch E-blast that went out regarding missing neighborhood
autistic child; as a result, the child was found within an hour. He commended their ability to get
this information out to mobilize community.

MPT Goodhart reported on his participation in the Police Unity Tour fundraising cycling event for
a national law enforcement memorial in Washington, DC, to recognize fallen officers who have
lost lives in line of duty. He said police officers keep us safe, as much as soldiers keep our country
safe; it is important to remember police officers in uniform also pay with their lives.

MPT Goodhart reported that he will participate in the League of California Cities conference on
environmental policy on June 14th in Sacramento. He reported on his attendance on Saturday, May
19th, at the PV Breakfast Club, which is celebrating their 70th Anniversary.

Councilmember Perkins reported on her attendance at the Capitol Comes to Campus event at PV
High on the 18th and 19th; low voter turnout and getting people more actively involved in the
community was discussed. She reminded voters that the Presidential Primary Election is on
Tuesday, June 5th.

She announced that Paul Taylor, MTA Deputy CEO, will make a presentation at the South Bay
COG Board of Directors Meeting of June 28th to explain the Feuer bill (AB1446), legislation to
extend the Measure R (transportation sales) tax.

Councilmember Perkins attended the South Bay Distinguished Speakers series on May 21st; Dan
Buettner spoke regarding longevity in other countries and what cities and policymakers can do to
promote healthier lifestyles in the community.

ADJOURNMENT

Mayor Bird adjourned the meeting at 8:20 p.m. to Thursday, May 24, 2012, 7:30 a.m. for the
purpose of an Adjourned Regular Meeting to conduct a Budget Study Workshop.
